rv.q: It's hard to warm to a production so lacking in verve and energy.
But this adaptation is a palpable miss...the character feels overexposed here, which really drains the book's brilliant final scene of power.

Hamnet is the latest book adaptation to hit Theatres and this story of the mostly undocumented family of William Shakespeare is a literary success, but can the theatrical version live up to these heights?
While William Shakespeare used almost 30,000 words in his art, so much is left unsaid in this production.

cn.t: Critics find this RSC adaptation of Maggie O'Farrell's bestseller disappointing, lacking the verve and emotional power of the source material, with too much left unsaid despite the novel's literary success.
